description: Proves every invalid input is refused with exit 2 before anything is read or changed, and that a machine without WireGuard for Windows (the runner) reports NOT_INSTALLED with exit 3 and changes nothing. Then it plants a fake wg.exe (printing handshake times from a file) and a do-nothing service named like a tunnel, both compiled on the runner, and walks every decision: no service, healthy, stopped, far end down, cooldown, always, and Disabled. Only a restart of a real tunnel with a real peer stays Tier 2.

No WireGuard for Windows on the runner: NOT_INSTALLED, nothing changed
No cooldown stamp written
Plant a fake wg.exe: WireGuard installed, no tunnel service
Tunnel deactivated in the WireGuard app (no service): NOT_ACTIVE, not activated
Plant a running fake tunnel service whose peer handshaked just now
Healthy tunnel: HEALTHY, left alone
Stop the tunnel service
Tunnel service stopped: restarted, handshake confirmed
The peer last handshaked an hour ago
Far end down: restarted, STILL_UNHEALTHY
Again inside the cooldown: COOLDOWN, not restarted
The peer handshakes again
Always inside the cooldown: restarted anyway
The peer is stale and the tunnel service is set to Disabled
Tunnel service set to Disabled: NOT_ACTIVE, not started

Tier 2 (a runner has no real tunnel or peer; the steps above use a fake wg.exe and service): a real tunnel whose service is stopped is restarted, re-reads its configuration and the real peer handshakes again
